input.rationale: Correcting a mechanism premise in my own knowledge before it propagates further. The recorded entry said the invocation sends on a nil channel when the gate is disarmed. Re-reading the source: stepWithWaitOption sends on n.propc, the always non-nil channel field (node.go:525), while the nil-ness lives in the run loop's local gate variable (node.go:344, assigned at 374/377/426 and used as the receive case at 386). The caller therefore blocks because the run loop is not receiving from that channel, not because the channel itself is nil. This matters for the resumption condition: the pending invocation is admitted as soon as the gate is re-armed by an observed leader change, so the non-completion lasts exactly as long as no leader change is observed (or until the caller's context or node stop), which is narrower and more precise than the recorded wording, and the interpretations that repeated the nil-channel phrasing need the corrected premise.

knowledge.statement: node.Propose and node.ProposeConfChange hand a MsgProp to the run loop through stepWithWaitOption, which sends the request on the node's proposal channel n.propc (an unbuffered channel field that is always non-nil) and, when the call waits for a result, blocks until the run loop accepts the request or the caller's context or the node stop ends the wait. The run loop only receives from that channel while its own local gate variable is armed (set when an observed leader exists, cleared when the local member is removed and when no leader is observed), so while the gate is disarmed the caller's send is pending: it returns context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded or ErrStopped only via those two exits, and it is admitted unmodified as soon as the gate is re-armed by an observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop (node.go) with the local proposal gate disarmed, e.g. after the local member was removed by a committed conf change and before any observed leader change; caller either supplies a deadline or a context that never expires.
knowledge.changed_premise: Previously recorded as 'when that channel is nil the send case cannot be selected'. The channel is not nil: the caller sends on n.propc (node.go:525) and blocks because the run loop's local gate variable is nil, so the receive case at node.go:386 cannot proceed until the gate is armed. Consequence for the claim: the pending invocation is admitted when the gate is re-armed (an observed leader change), so the non-completion window is bounded by the absence of an observed leader change rather than by the caller's context alone.

interpretations.rationale: Three retained executions agree; the mechanism statement is corrected in this revision, the evidence is unchanged. In 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4: node 3 applied its own re-admission (index 4: change add, ok true, voter true, leader 1, term 1) and its configuration listed it as a voter with leader 1 (index 5); the admitted invocation (index 6) had not returned after 1200 ms (index 7: returned false, err empty, voter true, leader 1), released only when the caller's deadline expired (index 8: 'context deadline exceeded', 2501 ms), and left its payload absent from every node's committed entries (index 9: present false, observed_nodes null). During the same stable-leader period the never-removed member's invocation returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 11, 12). Two independent retry attempts on node 3 (distinct operation ids, 900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also never completed (indices 14 and 19: returned false at 800 ms and 801 ms, voter true, leader 1) and were not committed, while in each of those intervals a fresh proposal by node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes (indices 17 and 22). After node 3 observed the leader change 1->2 at term 2 (index 23) the same call returned in 0 ms and committed on all three nodes (indices 25, 26). Source account, corrected: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; a re-admission cannot match the removal guard because the local Progress entry is already gone (node.go:401-412), so the gate stays disarmed and the caller's send on n.propc (node.go:525) stays pending until the caller's context, the node stop, or an observed leader change re-arms the receive side. The snapshot's own expectation (node_test.go:352-385) scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader and expects acceptance once a leader is known, which is the condition node 3 satisfies while pending; the control and interval controls exclude cluster-wide stalls, and the post-leader-change call excludes a defect in node 3's own state machine. Net effect: a member's proposal duty is held pending, without any error signal, for as long as no leader change is observed, and is admitted unmodified once one is.

investigations.question: After a voter is removed and then re-added by committed configuration changes, which code path lets a Node.Propose invocation on that re-added voter reach a decision (forward to the leader, be appended, or return an error), while the same leader stays in place?
investigations.hypothesis: node.run() disarms the proposal channel when the local member is removed (propc = nil) and only re-arms it on an observed leader change, so a re-admitted voter with a stable leader accepts Propose calls into a nil channel that never fires: the invocation neither forwards the proposal nor returns an error until the caller's own context expires.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a real three-node Node-API cluster (config {1,2,3}, leader 1) through committed remove-3 and add-3 conf changes, then invoke Propose on node 3 and on a never-removed member (node 2) with the same leader, and record whether each invocation returns, with which error, and whether its payload reaches any node's committed entries; finally force a leader change and repeat the invocation on node 3.

gaps.question: Besides an observed leader change, which source path re-arms the node.run() proposal gate for a member that is added back to the configuration, and which component is responsible for doing so?

knowledge.statement: node.run() keeps a local proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change: when r.lead changes and a leader exists it sets propc = n.propc, when no leader exists it sets propc = nil, and after applying a conf change that removes the local node from the configuration it sets propc = nil. Applying a conf change that adds the local node back does not change the gate (the removal branch is guarded by okBefore && !okAfter, which is false for a re-addition), so the gate stays nil until the next observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API (node.run loop) with a single goroutine consuming Ready and calling ApplyConfChange for every conf change entry in Ready.CommittedEntries; the local node is a voter that sees a leader, is removed by a committed conf change, and is then re-added by a later committed conf change, with the same leader in place throughout.

knowledge.statement: node.Propose and node.ProposeConfChange send a MsgProp to the run loop through stepWithWaitOption. For MsgProp the channel used is n.propc; when that channel is nil the send case cannot be selected, so the call blocks until the caller's context is done or the node is stopped, and returns context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded or ErrStopped instead of a proposal outcome.
knowledge.conditions: Same run loop as @gate with the proposal gate left nil; caller supplies a context whose deadline is reached while the node keeps running.

knowledge.statement: The raft state machine itself does not block a proposal from a member that is no longer in its own configuration: stepLeader returns ErrProposalDropped when the leader has no progress entry for itself (a removed leader), so the blocking behavior of a re-added voter is produced by the node wrapper's gate rather than by the state machine's proposal rules.
knowledge.conditions: State-leader step function with r.trk.Progress[r.id] == nil (local node removed from the active configuration).

knowledge.statement: The captured node-level test defines the intended proposal-blocking condition as 'does not know who is the current leader': it asserts that a Propose invocation on a node without a leader does not return, and then asserts that after the node campaigns and installs a leader the same pending invocation returns NoError. The test therefore scopes intended blocking to the unknown-leader case and expects acceptance once a leader is known; it exercises no removal/re-addition path and does not cover a member that is re-added while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter test node driven through the async Node API (newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1)), newNode + go n.run()); the assertion is on the invocation issued before any leader is known, and on the same invocation once the node becomes leader.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-node scenario, invocations on the re-added voter never completed and never delivered while other members' proposals were committed in the same intervals: invocation 1 (2500 ms context) had not returned after 1200 ms and released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at 2501 ms with no node holding its payload; retries 2 and 3 (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also had not returned and their payloads were absent, and in each retry interval a proposal by never-removed node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes. After the leader changed from 1 to 2 at term 2, the same invocation on the re-added voter returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks delivered; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged throughout the non-completing invocations; each retry uses an independent context and operation id.

interpretations.rationale: Source account: node.run() arms propc only through the observed-leader-change branch (node.go:373-377) and disarms it after applying a removal conf change (node.go:412-427); the re-admission case never matches that guard because okBefore is false once the local Progress entry was dropped, so subsequent proposals are enqueued onto a nil channel inside stepWithWaitOption (node.go:514-552) and can only end by context expiry or node stop. knowledge.statement: node.run() keeps a local proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change: when r.lead changes and a leader exists it sets propc = n.propc, when no leader exists it sets propc = nil, and after applying a conf change that removes the local node from the configuration it sets propc = nil. Applying a conf change that adds the local node back does not change the gate (the removal branch is guarded by okBefore && !okAfter, which is false for a re-addition), so the gate stays nil until the next observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API (node.run loop) with a single goroutine consuming Ready and calling ApplyConfChange for every conf change entry in Ready.CommittedEntries; the local node is a voter that sees a leader, is removed by a committed conf change, and is then re-added by a later committed conf change, with the same leader in place throughout.

knowledge.statement: node.Propose and node.ProposeConfChange hand a MsgProp to the run loop through stepWithWaitOption, which sends the request on the node's proposal channel n.propc (an unbuffered channel field that is always non-nil) and, when the call waits for a result, blocks until the run loop accepts the request or the caller's context or the node stop ends the wait. The run loop only receives from that channel while its own local gate variable is armed (set when an observed leader exists, cleared when the local member is removed and when no leader is observed), so while the gate is disarmed the caller's send is pending: it returns context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded or ErrStopped only via those two exits, and it is admitted unmodified as soon as the gate is re-armed by an observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop (node.go) with the local proposal gate disarmed, e.g. after the local member was removed by a committed conf change and before any observed leader change; caller either supplies a deadline or a context that never expires.

history.statement: node.Propose and node.ProposeConfChange send a MsgProp to the run loop through stepWithWaitOption. For MsgProp the channel used is n.propc; when that channel is nil the send case cannot be selected, so the call blocks until the caller's context is done or the node is stopped, and returns context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded or ErrStopped instead of a proposal outcome.

knowledge.statement: The raft state machine itself does not block a proposal from a member that is no longer in its own configuration: stepLeader returns ErrProposalDropped when the leader has no progress entry for itself (a removed leader), so the blocking behavior of a re-added voter is produced by the node wrapper's gate rather than by the state machine's proposal rules.
knowledge.conditions: State-leader step function with r.trk.Progress[r.id] == nil (local node removed from the active configuration).

knowledge.statement: The captured node-level test defines the intended proposal-blocking condition as 'does not know who is the current leader': it asserts that a Propose invocation on a node without a leader does not return, and then asserts that after the node campaigns and installs a leader the same pending invocation returns NoError. The test therefore scopes intended blocking to the unknown-leader case and expects acceptance once a leader is known; it exercises no removal/re-addition path and does not cover a member that is re-added while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter test node driven through the async Node API (newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1)), newNode + go n.run()); the assertion is on the invocation issued before any leader is known, and on the same invocation once the node becomes leader.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-node scenario, invocations on the re-added voter never completed and never delivered while other members' proposals were committed in the same intervals: invocation 1 (2500 ms context) had not returned after 1200 ms and released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at 2501 ms with no node holding its payload; retries 2 and 3 (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also had not returned and their payloads were absent, and in each retry interval a proposal by never-removed node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes. After the leader changed from 1 to 2 at term 2, the same invocation on the re-added voter returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks delivered; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged throughout the non-completing invocations; each retry uses an independent context and operation id.

interpretations.rationale: Source account: node.run() arms propc only through the observed-leader-change branch (node.go:373-377) and disarms it after applying a removal conf change (node.go:412-427); the re-admission case never matches that guard because okBefore is false once the local Progress entry was dropped, so subsequent proposals are enqueued onto a nil channel inside stepWithWaitOption (node.go:514-552) and can only end by context expiry or node stop. The state machine would have accepted the proposal (stepFollower forwards to the leader) and the removed-leader case returns ErrProposalDropped instead of blocking (raft.go:1298-1302), so no rejection or loss is reported to the caller while the member is in fact a voter with a known leader. The submitted experiment is the discriminator for this account and its retained receipt is expected to witness the invocation interval; this entry is currently a source-only account and will be revised with that receipt (including the control on a never-removed member and the post-leader-change invocation).

The same call on never-removed node 2, same leader 1, returned in 0 ms (index 11) and its payload was committed on all three nodes (index 12); the same node 3 call returned in 0 ms (index 15) and committed on all three nodes (index 16) once node 3 observed leader 2 after the forced campaign (leader change 1->2 at term 2). The source account explains exactly this difference: the run loop's proposal gate is assigned only at node.go:374 (observed leader exists), node.go:377 (no leader) and node.go:426 (local member removed), and the re-admission conf change cannot match the removal guard because okBefore is false once the node's own Progress entry was deleted (node.go:401-412), so MsgProp is enqueued onto a nil channel in stepWithWaitOption (node.go:525) and can end only via the caller's context or node stop. 3592ccaf01864f56aaf06d54a3f97423-gap-0.explanation: There is no such path in the captured snapshot.
